correctness.rationale: The nonempty signature of each private leaf forces selection from its disjoint root-leaf pair. Separation of each root from its private leaf forces the selected roots to total-dominate. Every remaining cross-pair is then separated except two roots whose private leaves are both omitted; they collide precisely when closed twins in the selected-root induced graph. This proves necessity and sufficiency. Independent coefficients arise by factoring zero-or-one omitted leaf per twin class. The zero case and all quantifiers hold. An independent direct closed-neighborhood signature test agreed on 1,860,132 subset tests across 1,239 graphs, and complete/star formulas were separately checked. The infinite proof is combinatorial, not experimental.

value.rationale: This is an exact full-cardinality invariant for every finite base graph after a natural one-leaf operation, not an arbitrary finite slice. The necessary-and-sufficient structural classification isolates a total-domination condition and a nontrivial induced true-twin correction, so it computes all feasible fault-identification code counts, total counts and a natural minimum-size coefficient. It extends known minima, without falsely asserting a faster algorithm or a journal-scale result.
